messages:
mira: Hey — I see a 500 for request_id=0a3b9f in the console but when I jump to pod logs I can't find any matching lines. I do have a trace id: trace-98765. What's the fastest way to chase the full request log (console -> CLI flow)?

sam: start with the trace UI: open the trace, look for span attrs named request_id / x-request-id / http.request_id. That often gives you the pod/span that emitted the log. If the trace has a `k8s.pod.name` attribute you can skip straight to stern/kubectl.

mira: opened trace-98765, the UI shows spans but no pod name column for a few spans. It's sparse for some hops.

raj: if UI misses it, download the raw trace JSON and jq it. e.g.:
```
curl -s 'https://tracing.internal/trace/trace-98765?raw=1' > /tmp/trace.json
jq -r '.spans[] | select(.attributes.request_id=="0a3b9f") | .attributes["k8s.pod.name"]' /tmp/trace.json
```
That prints pod name(s) if present.

sam: alternatively, grep the edge/ingress logs for the request id and then correlate to pod. Quick CLI:```
stern -n prod "edge-proxy|ingress" --since 20m | grep 0a3b9f -C 3
```
That usually finds the proxied request id in the same line as the upstream pod target.

mira: tried stern against edge-proxy but no hits. Is it possible request_id was only attached downstream?

taylor: yes — sometimes edge only sets upstream headers. Check the edge proxy access logs (different logger). Also try `kubectl logs` for pods matching the time window:```
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=edge-proxy -o name | xargs -I{} kubectl logs {} --since=30m | grep 0a3b9f -C2
```

raj: if all else fails, look at our logging pipeline index. For GCP: `gcloud logging read 'jsonPayload.request_id="0a3b9f"' --limit 50` — adapt for whatever cloud. The console search bar can do the same: set time range +/- 5m and search `request_id:"0a3b9f"`.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary rollout edge-proxy v1.4.2 started at 2024-06-12T15:32:00Z :rocket:

mira: ah — deploy happened ~15m before the error. Maybe logs rotated or pod restarted. Good catch.

sam: in that case, look for older pod names (terminated). Use `kubectl get pods -n prod --show-all --field-selector status.phase!=Running` or just `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep edge-proxy` — sometimes the log is in a terminated pod. Stern can follow terminated containers with `--all-namespaces`? (it streams live only).

raj: also check the trace span attributes for `span.link` or `resource.service.name` — that points to which service emitted the 500. Once you have service name, filter logs by that service label.

mira: I grabbed the raw trace and ran the jq snippet — it returned `edge-proxy-79b4d`. Used `kubectl logs edge-proxy-79b4d -n prod --previous` and found the 500 stacktrace. Thanks!

sam: nice. For follow-up, might be worth raising the 5xx alert to ignore post-deploy flakiness for 5m, we keep getting pages for canary flaps.

taylor: agree — can open a quick PR to bump the alert window or add a deploy-suppression. I'll file a ticket.

mira: filing a short incident doc now and linking the logs. Resolving for this thread — thanks all. :white_check_mark:
